$comment: Desired server-side protection for the branches this repository merges into. This file is the reviewable, revertible record of a configuration that otherwise lives only in GitHub's settings UI, where a change leaves no diff and no author. Apply it with `bash scripts/apply-branch-protection.sh --apply`; check for drift with `--verify` (which is what the scheduled audit runs). Rationale for each field: docs/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md.

required_status_checks.$strict_comment: Require the branch to be up to date before merging, so a policy that passed against a stale base cannot slip through.

main.$required_signatures_comment: Server-side commit signing. Turn this on only after docs/COMMIT_SIGNING.md enrolment is complete and the signed-commits rule has been at `warn` long enough to show a clean measurement; enabling it early blocks every contributor at once.
main.$enforce_admins_comment: Deliberate, and documented in docs/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md#administrator-override. Admins can bypass required checks so a production incident is not gated behind a twenty-minute Playwright run. The cost is that the bypass is possible at all, which is why every use is logged and reviewed rather than silent.

merge_queue.$comment: Two individually passing pull requests can combine into a broken main — that is precisely what produced the dropped-declarations merge. The queue tests the combined result before it lands.

main.$allow_auto_merge_comment: PR #96 merged before its CI run reported. Auto-merge is off; the merge queue is the supported path to unattended merging, and it waits for checks to report rather than to be requested.
